title: Workflow document
description: One named, ordered exchange between a protocol's participants: workflows/<name>.yaml. Flat message steps by default, three named fragment forms for structure, nothing else. Specified in framework/spec/kinds/protocol.md; parsed by framework/portal/src/lib/protocol/workflow.ts.

$schema.description: The dialect discriminator (0015-artifact-dialects); the canonical value is this schema's own $id. Deliberately unpinned rather than const: a value naming some other dialect is W_ARTIFACT_DIALECT, a warning, read as the legacy dialect and never broken — a const here would restate that ruling as a hard rejection in the one place a severity cannot be relaxed. The loader strips the key before parseWorkflow is handed the document, so nothing in the catalog depends on the parser tolerating it. parseWorkflow admits it regardless: workflowFileSchema is still a strict object and now carries $schema as an optional non-empty string at the root and nowhere else, so a caller holding raw file bytes and no loader — a fixture, an editor, a consumer reading this schema — gets the legacy dialect read rather than E_PROTO_WF_SCHEMA on the header this schema tells them to write. This format has no x- hatch and the header did not smuggle one in: one framework-owned literal was added to an enumerable set of root keys, so a misspelled steps: is still an error where an open extension point would have swallowed it.

participants.description: Lifeline order. A layout hint, never a restriction: an alias used in a step but not listed here is appended after the listed ones. MUST be a subset of the protocol's own participant aliases (E_PROTO_WF_ALIAS).

alias.description: A participant alias declared in the protocol's index.md. The alias namespace is the protocol's, never the workflow's.

steps.description: Every steps list — the workflow's own and every fragment's — MUST hold at least one step (E_PROTO_WF_EMPTY_BRANCH).

step.description: Exactly one discriminator key from message, alt, opt, loop (E_PROTO_WF_STEP_SHAPE). `otherwise` is the one permitted companion key, and only alongside `alt`. Steps have no ids: the portal's stable key is the positional path, e.g. steps[4].alt[0].steps[2].

message.description: Logical message name; the arrow label.

to.description: One alias, or a list of aliases when kind is event. A list on a non-event step is E_PROTO_WF_FANOUT. from and to MAY be the same alias — a self-call.

payload.description: An SRN reference that MUST resolve to a datamodel (E_PROTO_PAYLOAD_KIND) and SHOULD carry an @version pin — this is one of the few places a pin can still live, since a schema URL cannot carry one.

channel.description: Topic, queue, routing key or path. Cross-checked against the transport's surface list when one exists (W_PROTO_WF_CHANNEL_UNKNOWN); the check is skipped entirely when transport.yaml is absent or links an external spec instead.

condition.description: A display-only guard label on one arrow. It creates no branch — this is the most common authoring mistake in the format, and alt or opt is what changes the sequence.

alt-step.title: alt
alt-step.description: Mutually exclusive branches. At least two compartments, counting otherwise as one (E_PROTO_WF_SCHEMA): alt with a single branch and no otherwise is an opt, and the two mean different things.

opt-step.title: opt
opt-step.description: A single conditional branch: the steps may be skipped.
